agenda: Letter dated 13 April 2014 from the Permanent Representative of the Russian Federation to the United Nations addressed to the President of the Security Council (S/2014/264)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our primary objective is to secure Council adoption of a balanced, purely humanitarian text addressing the urgent needs of civilians, safe evacuation corridors, and compliance with international humanitarian law without politicized recriminations or attribution of blame. The most contentious point will be our deliberate omission of condemnation of our special military operation, which Western members will argue ignores the root cause of the humanitarian crisis. Additionally, Western delegations will strongly resist language prohibiting the placement of military assets in civilian areas and the use of civilians as human shields, as these provisions directly scrutinize Ukrainian military tactics.

messages.Albania: Albania considers this draft resolution to be an utterly cynical attempt by the Russian Federation to instrumentalize the Security Council and distract from the brutal aggression it alone initiated against Ukraine. A credible humanitarian text cannot remain silent on the root cause of the crisis or create a false equivalence between the aggressor and the victim defending its people. Unless the text explicitly identifies Russian aggression and demands the immediate, complete, and unconditional withdrawal of all Russian forces from Ukraine, Albania will not support it.
messages.Brazil: Brazil recognizes the critical urgency of addressing the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Ukraine and safeguarding the civilian population in full respect of international humanitarian law. However, an effective humanitarian response is inseparable from an immediate cessation of hostilities and genuine diplomatic dialogue. We urge the penholder to incorporate a clear call for the cessation of hostilities and to foster genuine consensus among Council members.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution and appreciates the focus placed on addressing the urgent humanitarian situation, protecting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and facilitating humanitarian access. We emphasize that humanitarian operations must adhere strictly to the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, and that humanitarian issues should not be politicized. China stands ready to support all efforts that contribute to alleviating the humanitarian crisis and encouraging dialogue and peaceful settlement.
messages.France: France cannot endorse a cynical initiative that purports to address the humanitarian tragedy while deliberately ignoring its sole cause: the unprovoked and unjustified aggression committed by the Russian Federation against Ukraine. Any credible humanitarian resolution must explicitly demand that Russia immediately cease its offensive and withdraw all of its armed forces from Ukrainian sovereign territory. We will not allow the Security Council to be instrumentalized to mask the responsibility of the aggressor for the ongoing attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure.
messages.Gabon: Gabon is gravely alarmed by the rapidly deteriorating humanitarian catastrophe and the plight of civilians in Ukraine. However, a meaningful humanitarian text cannot decouple the suffering of civilians from the military hostilities that caused it. Unless the draft clearly addresses the cessation of hostilities and fully upholds the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Ukraine, Gabon cannot support the text and will abstain.
messages.Ghana: Ghana remains deeply distressed by the catastrophic humanitarian consequences of the conflict in Ukraine and notes that this crisis stems directly from the military action against Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. While we appreciate the inclusion of language safeguarding foreign nationals and civilians fleeing the violence, any credible humanitarian resolution must call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of forces. A text that fails to address the root cause of the humanitarian suffering cannot command our support.
messages.India: India remains deeply concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation and reiterates the urgent need for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a direct return to dialogue and diplomacy. Humanitarian action must remain guided by the foundational principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, and should not be politicized. In the absence of Council consensus, India's stance on this draft remains an abstention.
messages.Ireland: Ireland cannot support a draft text that cynically ignores the root cause of the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Ukraine: the unprovoked, unjustified, and illegal invasion launched by the Russian Federation. Any credible Council response on the humanitarian situation must explicitly demand that Russia immediately cease its military assault and withdraw all its forces from Ukraine's sovereign territory. We reject any attempt to draw a moral equivalence between the aggressor and the victim or to use this Council to deflect responsibility for ongoing violations of international humanitarian law.
messages.Kenya: Kenya remains deeply alarmed by the severe humanitarian suffering in Ukraine and firmly upholds the sovereignty, political independence, and territorial integrity of Ukraine. Any credible humanitarian resolution by this Council must explicitly address the root cause of this crisis and call for an immediate cessation of hostilities. In the absence of language addressing the ongoing military offensive and demanding an end to the fighting, Kenya cannot support the draft as currently formulated.
messages.Mexico: Mexico believes that any credible Security Council action on the humanitarian situation must address its root cause and call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, as proposed in the initiative Mexico has pursued alongside France. A text that ignores the ongoing military offensive cannot effectively protect civilians or resolve the urgent humanitarian crisis on the ground. Unless these essential elements are reflected, Mexico cannot support this draft.
messages.Norway: Norway cannot support a draft resolution on the humanitarian situation in Ukraine that deliberately ignores the reality on the ground and the sole cause of this suffering: Russia's unprovoked, unjustified, and illegal invasion of Ukraine. A genuine humanitarian response requires addressing the root cause, which begins with the Russian Federation immediately halting its offensive and withdrawing its troops. Without an explicit call for Russia to cease hostilities and withdraw, this text cannot serve as a credible basis for Council action.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates remains gravely concerned by the worsening humanitarian crisis in Ukraine and stresses that the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access must remain paramount and depoliticized. Council action on pressing humanitarian needs should ideally reflect unity and consensus rather than deepen existing divisions. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, full adherence to international humanitarian law, and an urgent return to constructive dialogue and negotiations.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: This text is an exercise in utter cynicism and an insult to the Council. The humanitarian catastrophe in Ukraine is the direct result of Russia's unprovoked, premeditated, and illegal invasion. If Russia genuinely cared about the humanitarian situation, it would immediately halt its attacks on civilians, end its bombardment of Ukrainian cities, and withdraw its forces from Ukraine.
messages.United States of America: It is the height of cynicism and hypocrisy for the Russian Federation—the sole perpetrator of this unprovoked and brutal invasion—to circulate a draft resolution on the humanitarian catastrophe it alone created, while refusing to acknowledge its own responsibility. The Council must not legitimize a text that establishes a false moral equivalence between the aggressor and the victim or includes insidious language aimed at deflecting blame for attacks on civilians. If Russia genuinely cares about the humanitarian situation, it does not need a resolution: it simply needs to stop bombing Ukrainian cities and immediately withdraw all its forces from Ukraine.

messages.Albania: Albania categorically rejects this draft resolution, which represents a cynical attempt by the aggressor to mask its own responsibility for the humanitarian catastrophe in Ukraine. Any meaningful humanitarian text must clearly identify the Russian Federation as the sole perpetrator of this war and demand an immediate, complete, and unconditional cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of its forces. We cannot and will not support a text that seeks to whitewash an unprovoked invasion through false equivalence.
messages.Brazil: Brazil appreciates the penholder's incorporation of language on dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes in the preambular section. However, we reiterate that an effective and meaningful response to the humanitarian catastrophe requires an unequivocal call for an immediate cessation of hostilities. Without this critical element and a broader consensus among Council members, Brazil will not be in a position to support the draft and will abstain.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution in its current form, as it addresses the urgent humanitarian needs in Ukraine and prioritizes the safety and protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. We emphasize the importance of upholding the principles of humanity, neutrality, and impartiality, and call upon the Security Council to focus on practical measures to alleviate suffering and facilitate dialogue. We appreciate the penholder's efforts to keep the focus squarely on the humanitarian dimension of the crisis.
messages.France: France condemns the cynicism of a draft resolution tabled by the aggressor State that deliberately conceals the true cause of the humanitarian catastrophe in Ukraine: Russia's brutal and unprovoked war. We cannot endorse a text that instrumentalizes humanitarian principles while Russian forces continue to bomb Ukrainian cities and kill civilians. Unless Russia ceases its hostilities, withdraws its armed forces, and abides by international humanitarian law, France will not support this initiative.
messages.Gabon: Gabon emphasizes that any humanitarian resolution must unequivocally uphold the principles of the UN Charter, including full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. Without a direct call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and clear reaffirmation of these fundamental principles, the draft remains insufficient to address the dire realities on the ground, and our delegation will not be in a position to support it.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the retention of non-discrimination safeguards for foreign nationals and students in OP7. However, we remain convinced that any meaningful humanitarian response must address the root cause of the crisis and demand an immediate cessation of hostilities. As the current text still fails to call for an immediate end to the military action creating this humanitarian catastrophe, Ghana cannot support the draft in its present form.
messages.India: India reiterates its grave concern over the humanitarian situation in Ukraine and underlines the critical necessity of an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to dialogue and diplomacy. While we appreciate the focus on humanitarian access and the safe evacuation of all civilians and foreign students, humanitarian resolutions must command broad Council consensus to be effective on the ground. Given the continued polarization and lack of convergence among Council members, India will abstain on the draft.
messages.Ireland: Ireland cannot support a draft that willfully ignores the root cause of this catastrophic humanitarian crisis: the unprovoked and unjustified invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation. A humanitarian resolution that fails to name the aggressor or demand an immediate end to the military assault and the complete withdrawal of Russian troops lacks both credibility and moral authority. If the penholder maintains its refusal to reflect these fundamental realities, Ireland will abstain on this text.
messages.Kenya: Kenya appreciates the penholder's inclusion of explicit protections against racial and national discrimination in operative paragraph 7 for foreign nationals and students fleeing the conflict. However, any meaningful humanitarian response must directly address the root cause of civilian suffering by demanding an immediate cessation of hostilities and full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine. In the absence of an unambiguous call to halt the military action driving this catastrophe, Kenya cannot support this draft and will abstain.
messages.Mexico: Mexico reiterates that any meaningful humanitarian response must address the root cause of the suffering and explicitly demand an immediate cessation of hostilities. A text that fails to call for an end to military operations and fails to recognize the circumstances creating this humanitarian catastrophe cannot be supported by our delegation. If these core concerns are not incorporated, Mexico will not be in a position to vote in favor.
messages.Norway: Norway reiterates that any credible Council action on the humanitarian situation in Ukraine must clearly state the root cause of the crisis: the Russian Federation's unprovoked and unlawful aggression. A text that fails to name the aggressor and ignores the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and total withdrawal of Russian forces is unacceptable. Given the penholder's refusal to incorporate these fundamental principles, Norway cannot support this draft.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates appreciates the penholder's focus on the dire humanitarian situation and the imperative to protect civilians. However, effective humanitarian relief on the ground requires genuine Council unity and an explicit call for an immediate cessation of hostilities to enable diplomatic progress. In the absence of broader consensus among Council members, this text cannot achieve the necessary collective impact.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom reiterates that this draft is a cynical attempt by the Russian Federation to mask the humanitarian catastrophe of its own making. A resolution that refuses to name the aggressor and fails to call for an immediate cessation of Russian military hostilities and full withdrawal of Russian forces is entirely unacceptable. We will not lend credibility to an effort designed to obscure the reality of Russia's unprovoked and unlawful invasion of Ukraine.
messages.United States of America: It is unconscionable that the Russian Federation seeks to use the Security Council to whitewash a catastrophic humanitarian crisis of its own making. A resolution on the humanitarian situation in Ukraine that fails to explicitly identify Russia as the sole perpetrator and fails to demand the immediate cessation of its unprovoked aggression is an insult to the Charter. Without these essential elements and the removal of cynical attempts to blame the victim, the United States will not support this draft.

before.Russian Federation:
Today, the Security Council is voting on the Russian draft humanitarian resolution on Ukraine. We submitted this draft because the humanitarian situation on the ground requires an urgent and principled response from the Council. 

Our draft contains all the standard provisions of humanitarian resolutions: calls for a negotiated ceasefire, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, unhindered humanitarian access, humanitarian pauses, and the evacuation of civilians without discrimination. It also explicitly demands that all parties desist from placing military equipment in residential areas and strictly prohibits using civilians as human shields. 

We regret that our Western colleagues have chosen to politicize the humanitarian track, demonstrating once again that the fate of the Ukrainian civilian population is secondary to their anti-Russian geopolitical agenda. A vote in favour of this text is a vote for concrete humanitarian assistance to people in need, whereas a refusal to support it demonstrates a complete disregard for the humanitarian situation on the ground. We call on all members of the Council to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.United States of America:
It is really unconscionable that Russia would have the audacity to put forward a resolution asking the international community to solve a humanitarian crisis that Russia alone created. The United States intends to abstain on this text because, to state the obvious, Russia does not care about the deteriorating humanitarian conditions or the millions of lives and dreams that the war has shattered. If it cared, it would stop fighting.

Russia is the aggressor, the attacker, the invader — the sole party in Ukraine engaged in a campaign of brutality against the people of Ukraine — and it wants us to pass a resolution that does not acknowledge its culpability. It is cynical and it is shameful. By calling for a ceasefire without demanding the full withdrawal of Russian forces, Russia is attempting to lock in its military gains and buy time to regroup.

Russia wants this Council to pretend that the humanitarian disaster unfolding across Ukraine is an act of nature, rather than a catastrophe manufactured entirely by Moscow. We will not play along. The international community sees right through this farcical effort to deflect accountability. If Russia is truly concerned about the humanitarian situation, there is a very simple solution: cease the attacks, withdraw its troops from Ukraine, and end this unprovoked and unjustified war.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania abstained in the vote on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. 

We abstained because we refuse to become complicit in a cynical maneuver to whitewash an unprovoked and premeditated act of aggression. The humanitarian catastrophe unfolding before our eyes in Ukraine is not the result of a natural disaster. It is entirely man-made, and it has a single author: the Russian Federation.

It is the Russian Federation that chose to launch a war of aggression against a peaceful, sovereign neighbor. It is Russian bombs and missiles that are pounding Ukrainian cities, demolishing residential neighborhoods, schools, kindergartens, and hospitals. Just days ago, we saw the bombing of the drama theater in Mariupol, where hundreds of civilians were sheltering, with the word “children” clearly painted on the ground and visible from the air. 

For the aggressor to come to this Council posing as a concerned humanitarian, pretending to care about the very civilians its forces are besieging, starving, and bombing, is the height of hypocrisy. One cannot set the house on fire and then offer to help extinguish the flames while continuing to pour gasoline on them. 

This draft resolution was a farce. It deliberately ignored reality by omitting any reference to the root cause of the humanitarian tragedy: Russia’s unprovoked military aggression against Ukraine. It failed to call for the immediate cessation of hostilities and the unconditional withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukrainian territory. 

No one around this table or in the wider international community is fooled by such tactics. Today’s vote sent a clear and unequivocal message: the Council will not be used as a platform for propaganda and distraction. 

The most effective, direct, and immediate way to end the humanitarian suffering in Ukraine is simple: Russia must stop the war, silence its guns, and immediately, completely, and unconditionally withdraw all of its military forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders.

Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. I would like to make the following observations to explain our vote.

China feels deeply pained by the continued escalation of the conflict in Ukraine, the increasing civilian casualties, and the massive numbers of refugees and displaced persons. We have always maintained that the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries should be respected, the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations should be upheld, the legitimate security concerns of all countries should be taken seriously, and all efforts conducive to the peaceful settlement of the crisis should be supported. 

An early ceasefire is the urgent expectation of the international community, and it is also China’s strong hope. While pushing for an early cessation of hostilities, the Security Council should also respond positively, pragmatically, and constructively to the humanitarian crisis. On the humanitarian issue in Ukraine, China has put forward a six-point initiative. We welcome any initiative or measure that can help alleviate and resolve the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine.

The draft resolution just voted upon emphasizes the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, humanitarian pauses, and the evacuation of civilians, which reflects the common appeal and urgent humanitarian needs of the international community. China’s vote in favour was based on our principled position on the humanitarian issue in Ukraine, as well as our earnest expectation that the Security Council would shoulder its responsibility and reach a consensus on addressing the humanitarian situation.

It is regrettable that the Council was unable to reach an agreement today. However, the international community's focus on the humanitarian issue in Ukraine must not stop, nor should its efforts to resolve the crisis cease. China calls on all parties concerned to strictly abide by international humanitarian law, minimize civilian casualties, protect civilian facilities, facilitate humanitarian access, and ensure the safety of foreign nationals. China will continue to actively facilitate peace talks, play a constructive role, and work with the international community to promote an early ceasefire and achieve a peaceful settlement of the conflict.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
France abstained in the vote on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. 

For nearly a month, Russia has been waging an unprovoked, unjustified, and brutal war of aggression against Ukraine, in flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and the fundamental principles of international law. The consequences of this aggression are catastrophic: thousands of civilians killed, cities besieged and bombarded indiscriminately, and millions of people forced to flee their homes, creating the fastest-growing refugee crisis in Europe since the Second World War.

In this context, Russia’s initiative in presenting a draft resolution on the humanitarian situation is a grotesque exercise in cynicism. Russia cannot pretend to care about the humanitarian crisis that it alone created, while its bombs continue to rain down on Ukrainian civilians, schools, and hospitals in Mariupol, Kharkiv, and across Ukraine. One cannot attack a sovereign country, deliberately destroy its civilian infrastructure, starve besieged populations, and at the same time present oneself as a champion of humanitarian law.

Together with Mexico, France worked tirelessly for weeks in this Council to achieve a draft resolution addressing the urgent humanitarian situation, demanding the immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians, and unhindered humanitarian access. We engaged constructively with all members. However, it quickly became clear that Russia would veto any text that accurately reflected the reality on the ground and called for an end to its aggression. 

Because the Security Council has once again been paralyzed by Russia's cynicism and obstruction, we have brought our initiative to the Emergency Special Session of the General Assembly, where all Member States of the United Nations can make their voices heard. 

France reiterates its demand that Russia immediately stop its offensive, withdraw all of its armed forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, and fully respect international humanitarian law. We will continue our steadfast support for Ukraine and its people.
after.Mexico:
Mexico abstained in the voting on the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation because we consider that, in the face of the grave humanitarian crisis in Ukraine, the Security Council must act with responsibility, coherence and a clear commitment to international humanitarian law.

For weeks, Mexico, together with France, led intense negotiations within this Council to build a draft resolution strictly focused on addressing the urgent humanitarian consequences of the conflict. Our initiative was clear and balanced: it demanded the immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the guarantee of safe and unhindered humanitarian access, in full respect of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine.

Regrettably, the lack of agreement within this Council made it clear that a draft resolution of that nature would not achieve consensus here. For that reason, and in order to prevent inaction from prevailing, France and Mexico decided to take our humanitarian initiative to the General Assembly, where all Member States of the United Nations have a voice and a vote.

The text that was submitted to a vote today does not reflect the reality on the ground, nor does it address the indispensable requirement to stop the hostilities that are causing the humanitarian suffering of millions of people. A humanitarian resolution cannot overlook the facts, nor can it omit an explicit and unequivocal demand for the cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of military forces.

Mexico reiterates its unwavering commitment to international law, the Charter of the United Nations, and the protection of civilians in armed conflict. We will continue to work tirelessly in all multilateral forums, particularly in the General Assembly, to ensure that the international community provides an effective, principled and immediate humanitarian response to the victims of this conflict.
after.Norway:
Norway abstained in the vote on the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation.

Let there be no doubt: Russia, and Russia alone, is responsible for the war in Ukraine and for the devastating humanitarian catastrophe unfolding before our eyes. It is cynical in the extreme for Russia to put forward a resolution ostensibly addressing the humanitarian crisis that it alone has caused, while its forces continue to bombard Ukrainian cities, kill innocent civilians, and destroy homes, hospitals, and critical infrastructure. 

If Russia genuinely cared about the humanitarian situation and the lives of civilians, it would do the one thing that would immediately end the suffering: stop its war of aggression, cease all hostilities, and withdraw all its military forces from the territory of Ukraine immediately, completely, and unconditionally. Russia must also comply with the legally binding provisional measures order issued by the International Court of Justice on 16 March.

International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties at all times. Civilians and civilian objects, including schools and medical facilities, must be protected. Rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access must be granted to all those in need, in full accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence. 

The Security Council cannot be used to whitewash an unprovoked, unjustified, and illegal invasion. Norway remains steadfast in its solidarity with the people of Ukraine, and we reaffirm our unwavering commitment to Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.
after.Russian Federation:
The vote that has just taken place has exposed everyone for whom the humanitarian track is merely an instrument to score political points and level baseless accusations against Russia. 

By failing to support our draft resolution, Council members have refused to endorse a text containing clear, practical humanitarian provisions: calls for a negotiated ceasefire to organize humanitarian pauses, safe evacuation corridors, unhindered humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. They refused to adopt a resolution that explicitly demands that the Ukrainian armed forces and nationalist battalions stop using civilians as human shields and cease deploying heavy military equipment in residential areas, schools, and hospitals. 

Our Western colleagues have once again demonstrated their complete disregard for the genuine needs of people on the ground, sacrificing humanitarian imperatives for the sake of their anti-Russian geopolitical agenda. 

We express our sincere appreciation to our Chinese colleagues, who took a principled stand and voted in favour of the humanitarian draft resolution. 

Notwithstanding the outcome of today’s vote and the attempts by Western countries to politicize the humanitarian issue, the Russian Federation will continue to do everything necessary on the ground to provide life-saving assistance, organize humanitarian corridors, and ensure the safety and evacuation of civilians.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom abstained on the draft resolution before us today.

Russia’s draft resolution was a cynical attempt to whitewash its brutal aggression against Ukraine and to exploit a catastrophic humanitarian crisis of its own making. 

For nearly a month, Russia has waged an unprovoked, premeditated and illegal war against a sovereign United Nations Member State. Russian forces have laid siege to Ukrainian cities, indiscriminately pounded residential neighbourhoods, schools and hospitals, and killed thousands of innocent civilians. In Mariupol and across Ukraine, innocent people are trapped without food, water, heating or electricity, subjected to relentless Russian bombardment. 

Yet today, Russia had the grotesque audacity to put forward a text that feigns concern for the humanitarian situation, while deliberately failing to mention that Russia alone is the cause of this suffering. It omitted the basic truth that there is only one aggressor and one victim in this war.

If Russia genuinely cared about the humanitarian situation and the lives of Ukrainian civilians, the path forward is straightforward: stop the indiscriminate shelling, end the sieges, allow immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and withdraw all Russian troops from Ukraine in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter.

We will not allow Russia to use the Security Council to whitewash its atrocities or to peddle disinformation while it continues its campaign of destruction. The international community has seen through this transparent ploy, as reflected in the vote today. The United Kingdom remains unwavering in its support for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Ukraine.
